name: Mi Burrito
why: A long burrito list that reaches cabeza, lamb and tripa carries the signature mark, but cheap burrito shops are common and this is a good version of one. One Willamette Week roundup is all I found, with nothing on the room or its history, so atmosphere and story sit low.
story: Mi Burrito keeps more than 30 burritos on the menu, from asada and pollo to milanesa and chile verde. About a dollar more gets you lamb, cabeza, pork belly or tripa, and you pick whole pinto, black or refried beans. In 2026 it still sold burritos for ten dollars or less.
tagline: Over 30 burritos and three kinds of beans
order: A cabeza or tripa burrito, about a dollar more than the standard ones, with your pick of whole pinto, black or refried beans.
flags: Single source: Willamette Week's ten-dollar burrito roundup, Mar 25, 2026. No own site or second press piece opened.
WW calls it a St. Johns institution, but 819 N Lombard St is near N Interstate, miles east of downtown St. Johns. Area kept as Piedmont from the candidate record; confirm the neighborhood.
A directory lists a Mi Burrito at 2747 N Lombard St, perhaps an older or second shop. WW's 2026 address is 819 N Lombard St.
A directory says it opened in 2015; not used. Founding year and owners unknown.
No description of the room found; the atmosphere mark is a guess.
Closes at 10 pm per WW, so not marked late. Prices as of Mar 2026.
Newest dated evidence it is open: WW, Mar 2026.

name: Sanguiche
why: Italian sandwiches are common, but this one comes with a real family story and a house spice rub. It is brand new, opening in February 2026, and the room is a few tables, so atmosphere stays middling.
story: The Spillettes started with a steak rub Billy worked out at a family dinner, sold it at the Gresham Farmers Market, then added a sandwich booth. In February 2026 the family, with roots in Campania and Sardinia, opened this small downtown shop, which the couple runs with their kids.
tagline: A family spice rub that grew into a sandwich shop
order: The classic Italian is the top seller; the Dimepiece steak sandwich uses the family rub. On Wednesdays, come early for cannoli filled that day, which sell out.
practical: A few tables inside, some outdoor seating
Made to order, so expect a short wait
Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free bread options
flags: Very new: the shop had its grand opening Feb 1, 2026, after a farmers market booth in 2025.
Single source: The Outlook feature (Mar 10, 2026). Own site sanguicheshop.com is named there but did not turn up in search and was not opened.
Hours from March 2026; the owners said they were considering evening hours, so check.
Open status rests on the March 2026 article; delivery listings suggest it is still running, but those are not sources.

name: Las Brasas
why: Costa Rican cooking is hard to find around here, and the owner has been on chicken duty since 1982, so uniqueness and story hold up. The room is a plain converted laundromat, it only opened in February 2026, and one local paper is all the press so far.
story: Jorge Zuniga started cooking chicken in 1982 at another restaurant named Las Brasas. He and his wife Zoraida opened Casa de Pollo down the block in 2005, later moved it to Lake Oswego, then took two years off. This Costa Rican rotisserie is the comeback, in a rebuilt former laundromat.
tagline: Costa Rican rotisserie in a former laundromat
order: The marinated rotisserie chicken, which you can watch turning from the counter, as a casado plate with rice and beans. Ask for Zoraida's chimichurri.
practical: At the corner of Division and Main
Ceviche on Fridays and Saturdays only
Whole roast chicken family meal available
hours: Mon-Sat 10 am-8 pm, Sun 11 am-5 pm (Gresham Outlook, Feb 2026)
flags: Single source: everything comes from the Gresham Outlook opening feature (Feb 16, 2026). No other press, own site or neighborhood blog found; Instagram is @lasbrasasgresham per that article (not checked).
Most recent dated evidence is that Feb 2026 article. The discovery note cites a Sep 2026 county inspection, but I could not find it within budget.
Open less than a year (opened Feb 5, 2026).
Hours are from the Feb 2026 article and not rechecked.
The article does not say where the 1982 Las Brasas was (probably Costa Rica); the story avoids saying.

name: Murata
why: Tatami rooms and a family owner since 1988 make it rarer than the average downtown Japanese spot, and the weekday lunch set keeps getting recommended. We found little story beyond the ownership date, and it is widely covered, so nobody would call it a secret.
story: This Japanese restaurant in the 200 Market office building has been owned by one family since 1988, and it holds a sushi bar and three tatami rooms. Guidebooks have long noted its crowd of locals and Japanese businesspeople, and Portland critics still put it on their best-of lists.
tagline: Three tatami rooms in a downtown office building
order: The weekday teishoku lunch: pick a protein, anything from sashimi to fried chicken, and it comes with rice, pickles and cucumber salad. Call a few days ahead if you want a tatami room. At dinner, critics say skip the set menus for nigiri a la carte.
practical: Parking validation in the 200 Market building garage
hours: Weekday lunch from 11:30 am, last call 1:30 pm; dinner Mon-Sat from about 5 or 5:30 pm to 8:30 or 9 pm; closed Sun (own site for lunch and Sunday; dinner times from Time Out and Portland Monthly listings, which disagree)
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

Still-open check is soft: I found no dated evidence from after Nov 2025. The own site is live with lunch specials and phone reservations (undated), Wikipedia (read Oct 2026) shows no closure, and its newest cited coverage is Time Out's 2025 best-restaurants list. A Time Out list titled 2026 came up in search but I could not confirm Murata is on it. Worth a call before approving.

Fit check: Time Out puts dinner at about $40 or more a head, and The Oregonian (2024, via Wikipedia) says weekend dinner tables are hard to get. Drafted as a lunch spot; you may judge it too reservation-driven for the guide.
Dinner hours differ between Time Out (5-8:30 pm) and Portland Monthly (5:30-9 pm) listings; the own site, seen only as a search snippet, confirms lunch last call 1:30 pm and closed Sundays.
Teishoku details and garage validation come from an undated Portland Monthly lunch guide, seen as a search snippet.
'Since 1988' is when the current family took ownership (Wikipedia citing Portland Monthly); the opening year was not found.
Heavily covered (Portland Monthly top 50 in 2024, The Oregonian, Eater Portland, Time Out, The Infatuation, Fodor's); local-legend would also be defensible.

name: Goose Hollow Inn
why: A tavern opened by a future mayor that gave the neighborhood back its name, still in his family, with a Reuben that is its whole reputation. It is on every list, and at heart it is a tavern with one famous sandwich, which keeps uniqueness out of the 90s.
story: Bud Clark bought Ann's Tavern at SW 19th and Jefferson in 1967 after the city razed his old bar, and named it to revive a lost neighborhood name. He went on to be mayor while his wife Sigrid ran the place. The Clark family still owns it, and the Reuben is the point.
tagline: A future mayor's tavern, family-run since 1967
order: The Reuben: corned beef and Reuben sauce, toasted on rye. Pair it with a pint and take it out to the deck under the birch trees.
practical: No video poker, just one TV
hours: Daily from 11 am, to midnight most nights and 1 am Fridays (Portland Monthly listing, undated)
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

No dated sign of life since Nov 2025 found within budget. The own site speaks in the present tense (still going strong, daughter Rachel manages) but is undated; the March 2026 travel guide in the discovery note was not seen.
Hours and `late` rest on an undated Portland Monthly listing (WW's 2015 bar guide had the same hours). Directory listings show 10 to 11 pm closings, so confirm before keeping `late`.
The discovery lead's 'Reuben goes through a pizza oven' was not confirmed by anything I could read, so it is left out.
The own site gives Bud Clark's mayoral term as both 1985-1992 and 1985-1993; the story avoids the years.
Story facts are mostly from the tavern's own site, backed on the naming and Reuben by WW and Wikipedia.

name: Devil's Dill
why: Being the city's late-night deli is a real niche in an early-closing town, and readers still vote for it. We found almost nothing about the room or a signature sandwich, and the story is mostly the hours.
story: Devil's Dill has made sandwiches on Hawthorne since 2013, and its name rests on serving them late: as of 2025 it was the city's only late-night deli. A second shop opened on NE Killingsworth in 2025, and Willamette Week readers ranked it second for late-night eats in 2026.
order: A hot sandwich after 10 pm, which is the whole reason people know it. Check the Hawthorne hours before you go, since they have moved around over the years.
hours: Sun-Tue until 11 pm, Wed-Sat until 1 am; opening time not confirmed (Wikipedia, as of 2025; own site lists no hours)
flags: Status unclear: the Hawthorne shop may be closed after a September 2026 fire in its building (Wikipedia, seen in search results). Confirm before approving.

Wikipedia (seen in search results) says a fire damaged the building housing the Hawthorne shop in September 2026. I could not confirm whether the shop is open now. The own site still offers online ordering from Hawthorne. Confirm before publishing.

Late hours (to 1 am Wed-Sat, 11 pm other nights) come from Wikipedia as of 2025, seen in search results only; the own site lists no hours. Older listings show 3 am closing (WW 2017). Re-check, especially after the fire.
Opening time unconfirmed from a usable source, so midday is left off `when`; directory listings show an 11 am opening.
No specific sandwich sourced; `order` rests on the late-night reputation.
Two locations, under the chain line: Hawthorne and NE Killingsworth (own site gives 1620 NE Killingsworth; Bridgetown Bites gave 5470 NE 16th Ave for the same shop).
Willamette Week 2026 readers' poll also lists it as a finalist for Best Sandwich Shop (July 22, 2026).

name: Cricket Cafe
why: A steady Belmont breakfast room with a genuine comeback story and a menu that works for mixed diets. Nothing here is one of a kind, and no usable source names a standout dish.
story: Cricket Cafe has been cooking breakfast on Belmont since 1999. It closed without warning in June 2017, then reopened under new owners who kept the menu mostly as it was and added more vegan and gluten-free plates.
order: Breakfast for a table with mixed diets, since the menu carries vegan and gluten-free versions alongside the usual plates. Come early on weekdays: the kitchen stops at 1 pm.
hours: Mon-Fri 8 am-1 pm, Sat-Sun 8 am-2 pm (own site)
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

No dated evidence that it is open since Nov 2025. The own site lists current hours and takeout but carries no date. Discovery cited Travel Portland's Belmont guide (said to be revised in 2026), which this environment can't open. Confirm it's open before publishing.

June 2017 closing, reopening under new owners and the added vegan and gluten-free dishes come from Wikipedia, Willamette Week (Oct 2017) and the Portland Mercury (Jan 2018) as seen in search results; I did not open those pages.
Most recent dated press found is from 2018.
No specific dish sourced. Reviews mention a vegan skillet, but only on sites we can't cite.
Older listings give different hours (daily to 2:30 pm in 2018); own site hours used.
